findings.domainNotFound: The domain does not exist. Check that it is spelled correctly.
findings.spfMissing: There is no SPF record: nobody can check which servers send legitimate email for this domain.
findings.spfMultiple: There is more than one SPF record. The standard requires a single one and receivers may discard them all.
findings.spfStrict: It ends in -all: anything that does not come from an authorised server is rejected.
findings.spfSoftfail: It ends in ~all: anything that does not come from an authorised server is marked suspicious but not rejected. That is common and enough if DMARC is in place.
findings.spfNeutral: It ends in ?all: it says nothing about unauthorised senders. Change it to ~all or -all.
findings.spfOpen: It ends in +all, or plain all: it authorises any server in the world. It is the same as having no SPF.
findings.spfNoAll: It does not end in all: unauthorised senders have no rule. Add ~all or -all.
findings.spfRedirect: It hands over to another domain with redirect=: that domain's rules apply.
findings.spfPtr: It uses ptr, which the standard discourages: it is slow and unreliable.
findings.spfTooManyLookups: It counts {count} DNS lookups from this record's mechanisms alone, and the limit is 10. Beyond the limit, receivers treat SPF as broken. Includes are not followed here, so there may be more.
findings.dmarcMissing: There is no DMARC record: nobody tells receivers what to do with email that spoofs this domain.
findings.dmarcInherited: The domain has no DMARC record of its own and inherits the one from {domain}.
findings.dmarcMultiple: There is more than one DMARC record. The standard requires a single one.
findings.dmarcInvalid: The record has no valid policy (p=none, quarantine or reject).
findings.dmarcReject: The policy is reject: email that spoofs the domain is rejected.
findings.dmarcQuarantine: The policy is quarantine: email that spoofs the domain goes to spam.
findings.dmarcNone: The policy is none: it only monitors and blocks nothing. Use it only while you review the reports, then move to quarantine or reject.
findings.dmarcSubdomainWeaker: Subdomains have a looser policy ({policy}) than the main domain.
findings.dmarcPartial: The policy applies to only {percentage} % of emails (pct).
findings.dmarcNoReports: It does not ask for reports (rua): you will not know who sends email on behalf of the domain.
findings.dkimMissing: There is no DKIM key with that selector. Check the selector in the DKIM-Signature header of a real email.
findings.dkimRevoked: The key is empty: the selector has been retired and signatures made with it will fail.
findings.dkimInvalid: The public key is not valid.
findings.dkimTestMode: It is in test mode (t=y): receivers should not treat a signature failure as final.

parcel.name: Express Parcels
parcel.subject: Your parcel could not be delivered: pay €1.99 to receive it
parcel.body:
Hello, customer:

We tried to deliver your parcel and nobody was home. To schedule a new delivery you must pay a €1.99 handling fee within the next 24 hours. After that, the parcel will be returned to the sender.

Thank you for trusting us.
parcel.explanation: It uses the fear of losing a parcel to make you pay and hand over your card details.

clues.1: The sender's address is not the company's: it is a .info domain with hyphens, bought for this.
clues.2: It rushes you for no reason: 24 hours or it goes back.
clues.3: It asks you to pay a small amount from a link. What they steal is the card, not the euro.
clues.4: The link goes to a different domain from the company's, ending in .top.

bank.name: Example Bank · Security
bank.subject: We have blocked your account
bank.body:
Dear customer:

We have detected suspicious access to your account. For your security, you must verify your details within the next 12 hours. If you do not, your account will be permanently suspended.
bank.explanation: It scares you with blocking your account so you type your username and password into a fake site.

clues.1: The sender's domain only imitates the bank's: it adds «security» to the name.
clues.2: It does not address you by name: «Dear customer».
clues.3: It threatens to suspend the account if you do not act within 12 hours.
clues.4: It wants you to type your details on a site you reach from a link in the email, and the link goes to a different domain.

invoice.name: Nubesur Billing
invoice.subject: Invoice 2024-0318 for your Hosting Pro plan
invoice.body:
Hello, Marta:

We attach the September invoice for your Hosting Pro plan, for €29.00. It will be charged on the 5th to the card ending in 4821.

You can view it any time in your customer area.
invoice.explanation: Everything fits a service you have signed up for, and it asks for nothing urgent.

clues.1: The link goes to the same domain as the sender: nubesur.es.
clues.2: It addresses you by name and gives concrete details: the plan, the amount and the last digits of the card.
clues.3: There is no rush or threat: it announces a normal charge. Even so, if in doubt, type the address in yourself.

director.name: Elena Martín (Management)
director.subject: Urgent and confidential
director.body:
I need you to make a €4,800 transfer today to a new supplier. I am in a meeting and cannot talk on the phone.

I will send you the IBAN as soon as you confirm. Do not tell anyone until I say so.
director.explanation: It is the «CEO fraud»: someone poses as management so you pay an account that belongs to no supplier.

clues.1: The name is the director's, but the email comes from a free service and not from the company's.
clues.2: It asks for urgency and secrecy at once, so nobody can check it.
clues.3: It wants a transfer to a new supplier, with no invoice or order.
clues.4: It says it cannot talk, which is exactly what would expose it. Confirm by calling the usual number.

password.name: IT Support
password.subject: You have changed your password
password.body:
We confirm that your password was changed today at 09:14 from Madrid.

If it was you, you do not need to do anything. If it was not you, type the intranet address in your browser, go to your profile and change it, or call support.
password.explanation: It reports something that happened and does not ask you to click or give any details.

clues.1: It has no link or attachment: there is nothing to click.
clues.2: If it was you, it asks for nothing. The alert exists for the opposite case.
clues.3: It tells you how to act on your own, typing the address yourself, and not with a link in the email.

prize.name: Market Prizes
prize.subject: Congratulations! You have won a latest-generation phone
prize.body:
You have been chosen among 10,000 users as the winner of our monthly draw.

To claim your prize, fill in the form with your details and your card details: that way we cover the shipping costs.
prize.explanation: A prize you did not enter for is bait to get your card details.

clues.1: You did not enter any draw.
clues.2: A free prize does not ask for your card to ship it.
clues.3: The sender ends in .xyz and the link goes to a different domain, also .xyz.
clues.4: It flatters you and picks you among thousands: that is the hook.

phishingQuiz.more: Want your team to practise with cases like these? Aegis runs awareness campaigns with tracking.

aiGovernance.title: AI governance
aiGovernance.intro: Ellysia uses artificial intelligence to write texts in three of its tools. This page explains, tool by tool, what the AI does, what data the model receives and how what it writes is marked.

faq.title: What is usually hard to decide

passwordsLeave.q: Do my passwords leave my browser?
passwordsLeave.a: No. Acheron encrypts in your browser before sending anything: the server only sees ciphertext and never receives your master password or the key derived from it.

lostMasterPassword.q: What happens if I lose my Acheron master password?
lostMasterPassword.a: The vault's content is lost, and there is no way to recover it. It is the direct consequence of the key never travelling: if we could give it back to you, we could also read your secrets. Keep it where you would keep your house key.

technical.q: Do I need to be technical to use it?
technical.a: To launch an analysis and read the report, no: you choose a target and receive the written result. Installing the Hygeia agent on a server does require access to that machine.

hygeiaAgent.q: What does the Hygeia agent need?
hygeiaAgent.a: A lightweight service on the machine you want to watch. It is the agent that sends data out every few seconds, so no inbound port needs to be opened.

cost.q: How much does it cost to start?
cost.a: Nothing. The entry plan is free, asks for no card and never expires. If you run short of quota, the paid plans are further up.

configView.lasCredencialesVivenEnEl: The credentials live in the {c1} file. These settings require restarting the API to apply.
configView.laContrasenaSeTomaDe: The password is taken from {c1} in {c2}. In containers, the {c3} / {c4} / {c5} variables take precedence over these values.
configView.eligeQueProveedorGeneraEl: Choose which provider generates each module's content. The credentials stay in {c1}; the model is chosen here and applies to the next background job, with no restart.
configView.laListaSaleDePreguntarle: The list comes from asking the provider what it serves right now. Leaving the field empty means using the environment variable, which is how it worked before the model could be chosen here.
configView.elTopeDeTokensRechaza: The token cap rejects an oversized prompt before spending the call. The circuit breaker stops calling the provider after the given consecutive failures, so as not to chain waits against a backend already known to be down.
configView.unModeloLocalTardaMucho: A local model takes much longer than a cloud API, so each provider has its own.
configView.porAquiSalenLasCampanas: Aegis campaigns, Hygeia and Iris alerts and account emails (verification, invitations, recovery) go out through here. The relay username and password live in {c1} and {c2} in {c3}; nothing here is secret.
configView.loQuePintanLasPlantillas: What the templates render. This is the product's base brand: per-organization white-labeling is configured in each organization and applied on top of it.
configView.puntuacionDeAutenticidadDeUn: Authenticity score of an email. Above the legitimate threshold it is considered trustworthy; below the suspicious one, a threat. The suspicious threshold can be negative.
configView.elEspejoLocalDeNvd: The local mirror of NVD, KEV, EPSS and OVAL that Lybra uses to decide whether a detected service is vulnerable. “Maximum age” is how much is tolerated since each source's last sync before warning that it is stale; it deletes nothing.
configView.cuantoEmpujaElMotorContra: How hard the engine pushes against the target. Raising concurrency or lowering the interval speeds up the scan and increases the risk of the target treating it as an attack.
configView.elTrozoDeRespuestaCruda: The chunk of raw response kept with each finding so it can be reviewed later.
configView.esLaUnicaFaseQue: This is the only phase that writes to the target: each attempt is a real sign-in. The cap is per account, not per service, and keeps the check from turning into brute force.
configView.descubreLoQueLosChecks: Discovers what the checks do not know beforehand: robots.txt paths, login forms and authenticated paths. Read-only and same-origin, with a hard budget. At zero pages, it is skipped.
configView.unActivoPasaADesconectado: An asset becomes “offline” when it misses the given number of consecutive heartbeats. Lowering the interval multiplies the data volume: retention decides how much history is kept.
configView.latidosSostenidosEvitaLasAlertas: “Sustained heartbeats” avoids alerts for a one-off spike: the metric has to stay high for that many consecutive heartbeats. Disk and swap alert on the first one.
configView.laPaletaConLaQue: The palette used to generate the Hygeia PDF, like each Themis scanner's.
configView.cuandoElAnalisisSeAtreve: When the analysis dares to state something. A trend that does not pass these thresholds returns no estimate: it steps back and says why, instead of giving a made-up date.
configView.cuantoTiempoSeReutilizaUna: How long an already computed statistic is reused before recomputing it. The longer the requested period, the slower the result changes. Registering or removing an asset or changing its tags discards that user's cached results.
configView.topesDeLoQueEl: Caps on what the agent can send and what the API accepts. Tightening them protects the API from a compromised or misconfigured agent.
configView.queFuncionesEstanAbiertasAl: Which features are open to the public
configView.escanerDeRedAnalisisWeb: Network scanner, web analysis and vulnerabilities
configView.cadaNocheSeArchivaEl: Every night the previous day is archived and anything older than this is deleted. The log stores the IP of each visit.
configView.elDeQuienNoHa: The one used by anyone who has not chosen a language and whose organization has not set one either.
configView.soloLaFamiliaHsLa: HS* family only: signing uses a symmetric secret
configView.cadaCuantoSeLeRecuerda: How often it is recalled to anyone who does not have it enabled
configView.vacioLasPlantillasQueTrae: Empty = the templates shipped with the application
configView.estrictoSubeLosDosUmbrales: Strict raises both thresholds by 5 points (alerts earlier); lenient lowers them by 5
configView.nombreDeLaCarpetaVirtual: Name of the virtual folder for ungrouped scans
configView.escaneosRecientesQueSePromedian: Recent scans averaged in the history
configView.pasadoEsePlazoUnHallazgo: After that period, an accepted finding counts again
configView.loQueEsperaLaCola: How long the queue waits before considering a scan dead
configView.cuantoHistoricoSePideEn: How much history is requested in each pass
configView.vacioLasQueTraeEl: Empty = the ones shipped with the binary
configView.loQueSeEscaneaSi: What is scanned if the user chooses nothing else
configView.formatoXYZUn: X.Y.Z format. An asset with an older version is marked as outdated in the list; "0.0.0" marks none.
configView.de0A1Cuanto: From 0 to 1. How closely the series must resemble a straight line to trust its direction; raising it leaves disks that grow in steps without an estimate
configView.porDebajoDeEstoSe: Below this the metric is considered to fluctuate, not to grow
configView.cuantoPuedenSepararseDosPicos: How far apart two peaks of different metrics can be and still count as simultaneous
